summary: Kangei Okamoto (1899–1948) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and archaeology. He studied under Takamatsu Yoshie and at the University of Paris, later serving as an appointee (嘱託) at the Tokyo Imperial Household Museum.

Kanoko Tanaka works in religious studies and Indology, having studied under the traditional teacher Acharya Tulsi. In 2001, she was attested as a part-time lecturer in religious studies at Komazawa University.
Kansei Tamura, a scholar of Buddhist studies, studied at the University of Tokyo and held a post as a lecturer at Rissho University (both attested 1962).

Kapila Vatsyayan (1928–2020) was an Indologist and historian. Educated at Delhi, Michigan, and Banaras Hindu University, she taught at Delhi and BHU, served as chairperson of the India International Centre, and held leadership roles at IGNCA (1987, 1993–2000, 2005).

Karel Werner (1925–2019) worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. Educated at Masaryk and Palacký universities, he taught at Palacký (~1947–1951), Cambridge (1968), Durham (1969–1990), and Masaryk (1993–1998), holding guest professorships in India, Sri Lanka, and South Korea.
Karen Cheatham is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned a master's degree from the Graduate Theological Union and a doctoral degree from the University of Toronto (attested 2007).

Karen Christina Lang works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at the University of Washington under David Seyfort Ruegg, at Banaras Hindu University, and the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, later serving as a professor at the University of Virginia.

Karen L. Brock is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. After earning her Ph.D. from Princeton University, she held assistant professorships in Japanese art at Washington University in St. Louis (attested 1988) and the University of Michigan (attested 1990).

Karen McCarthy Brown (1942–2015) was a religious studies scholar. She studied at Smith College, Union Theological Seminary, and Temple University (~1974–1976), and spent most of her career as a professor of anthropology at Drew University (~1976–2009).

Karen Nelson Villanueva is a religious studies scholar who earned her PhD from the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2013). She studied under traditional teachers Geshe Ngawang Dakpa and Lobsang Chökyi.
Karen Nero held academic posts at the University of Canterbury (~2002–2007) and the University of Otago, and she taught Sally McAra.

Karen O'Brien-Kop works in religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at SOAS University of London, where she also served as a senior teaching fellow, and was attested in 2020 as a lecturer at the University of Roehampton.

Karin Meyers works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied under Jay L. Garfield and served as assistant professor and MA program director in Buddhist studies at Kathmandu University's Centre for Buddhist Studies at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Karin Preisendanz (born 1958) is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. After earning her doctorate and Habilitation at the University of Hamburg, she held posts at Free University of Berlin, University of British Columbia, Hamburg, and the University of Vienna (1999).

Karl Ammer (1911–1970) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Vienna (~1930–1935). He served as a professor and Director of the Institute of Indology at the University of Halle (~1957–1970).

Karl Benedikt Hase (1780–1864) was a linguist and historian. After studying at Jena and Helmstedt, he held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (~1805–1864), the École des langues orientales (1816–1864), and the Faculty of Arts of Paris (1852–1864).

Karl Brugmann (1849–1919) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Halle and Leipzig under Georg Curtius. He held professorships at the University of Freiburg (1884) and Leipzig University (1882, 1887–1919).

Karl Brunnhölzl is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers including Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche, Tenga Rinpoche, Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche, Sangye Nyenpa Rinpoche, Ringu Tulku, and Khenpo Lama Thubten.

Karl Debreczeny is a scholar of Tibetology, history, archaeology, and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Wu Hung and Jennifer Purtle, and served as a curator at the Rubin Museum of Art (attested 2008).

Karl Eduard Zachariae von Lingenthal (1812–1894) was a historian. He studied at Leipzig, Berlin, and Heidelberg, later holding an academic post at Heidelberg University from approximately 1836 to 1842.
